newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat up late on commercial buying.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat up late on commercial buying.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures turned higher in late dealings on commercial buying, traders said.
As of 1253 CDT, Cargill Inc had purchased three million bushels of September and bought two million December, traders said.
The commercial demand led to talk that an export sale of U.S. wheat may have been made, the traders said.
Wheat was pressured in early dealings on a drop in corn and soybean futures.
Rain over the weekend in portions of the U.S. Midwest corn and soybean growing region and forecasts for more rain this week hit the corn and soybean markets, the traders said.

Some attention also may have been given to news Egypt's main wheat importer said he was not planning to buy wheat for up to a month until health officials solve issues raised by an import ban on genetically engineered grain.
But industry experts said last week that wheat for export was not genetically altered so there should be no problem with wheat exports to Egypt.
At 1256 CDT, wheat was two to 3-1/4 cents higher, with July up two at $3.30-1/2. Sep was up four at $3.40.
